questions.q: What does a semantic model add on top of raw tables like trips and zones?
options: Row-level security masks only, nothing else
A physical copy of every table, duplicated for reporting
Relationships between tables, measures (business calculations), and friendly names, so a report author queries concepts rather than raw columns
A completely new storage format replacing Delta
questions.explain: Without this layer, there's no agreed-on business definition — what counts as "revenue," for instance.

questions.q: When is a default semantic model created?
options: Only after a user manually configures one from scratch
Only after a report is published
Semantic models must be created before a Lakehouse can exist
Automatically, the moment a Lakehouse exists — no separate setup step required
questions.explain: This is similar in spirit to how a workspace already has somewhere for data to live before you ask for it.

questions.q: How does a relationship in a semantic model compare to a PySpark join()?
options: A relationship can only be defined inside a notebook, never in a semantic model
It connects two tables the same way a join does, except defined once in the model rather than repeated in every query
Relationships and joins are completely unrelated concepts
Relationships replace the need for any join ever again
questions.explain: This directly parallels Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 55's join() connecting the same two tables, but defined once instead of repeatedly.

questions.q: Why does defining a measure once matter, rather than each report author writing their own calculation?
options: Measures are automatically generated with no user input needed
It has no real benefit; it's purely a stylistic convention
Measures can only be defined once per Fabric tenant, technically
It avoids the risk of two different report authors defining the same business concept (like "Total Revenue") differently
questions.explain: A named, reusable calculation avoids that exact kind of definitional drift across reports.

questions.q: Where does Direct Lake mode (from Lesson 12) actually live?
options: It's a property of the semantic model itself, not a report-level setting
It's a setting only configurable per individual report
It's a property of the Lakehouse's storage account
Direct Lake mode has no connection to semantic models at all
questions.explain: A model built in Direct Lake mode is what lets reports built against it read Delta's Parquet files directly.
